acceptance_checks: New e2e case where the stubbed check status is a real function of the PR head and the stub runner writes a fix: the loop history is [dispatch_repair, ..., merge] with outcome complete, not stop_guardian.
After that run the repair worktree has commits beyond its base and the origin branch tip moved.
When the push fails the loop returns stop_blocked naming the failure and does not silently consume a repair attempt.
A generated repair packet contains an Evidence Required section including the push instruction and a Prohibited line matching the task handoff's commit/push prohibition.
test_shiki_p2_repair_limit.sh stays green (the cap still applies when repairs genuinely do not fix the check).
A completed repair updates its PR head with no operator git command.
non_goals: Changing repair-packet contents beyond rendering evidence_required
scope:
In execute_action's dispatch_repair branch in scripts/shiki_loop.py, call the existing _commit_and_push_implementation after _dispatch_repair returns, record its result, and fail closed to stop_blocked when it does not report a push — exactly as the create_pr branch already does. Render the repair packet's evidence_required in cmd_handoff_repair and add the same 'the goal loop owns commit/push' prohibition the task handoff carries, so the runner's contract is unambiguous in both directions.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes. On 2026-07-27/29 a single task was driven from Goal to PR twice (#179, merged; #181, open at the time of writing). The loop's judgments were autonomous; the plumbing between them was not. Seven manual interventions were required, and this task removes one of them.
  Manual step removed: committing and pushing a completed repair by hand, because dispatch_repair delivers nothing.
  Observed: repair RP-20260729T051350511459Z-50b5c0d7 finished correctly in the worktree and PR #181 did not move; the coordinator had to commit and push the loop's own work.
  Reproducible when: a repair that finishes green updates its PR without an operator running git, and a push failure stops the loop with a named reason instead of silently consuming a repair attempt.
test_command: bash scripts/test_shiki_loop_e2e.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_p2_repair_limit.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
title: Deliver the repair to the PR
